gitCommit.subject: Detect self-cancelling card pairs by amount, not by wording
gitCommit.body:
Detect self-cancelling card pairs by amount, not by wording

Replaces the CARGO TRASPASADO regex committed earlier. That approach was wrong
twice over, and production data showed both.

It was too narrow. Across every user, positive rows on credit accounts arrive as
"ABONO CARGO TRASPASADO CCUOTAS", "PAGOS CON PUNTOS", "CASHBACK", "VISA SHOPPING
DAYS" and bare merchant refunds. A regex covers one bank's phrasing and fails
silently on the rest.

And its representation was unsafe. Storing the credit as a positive-amount
variable_expense violated "expenses = negative" from CLAUDE.md, defended by
nothing: transaction_row_controller derives the sign from the type and fires on
any dirty field, so editing the description of one of those rows flipped +2210 to
-2210 and doubled the ZARA charge.

Matching on amount instead. On a credit account, a positive row that exactly
cancels a negative row in the same statement is a self-cancelling pair. Of 53
positive rows across 18 credit accounts, exactly four matched — three reversals
re-billed as meses sin intereses, and one purchase settled with points. All four
should cancel. None of the 48 card payments matched anything, which is the
false-positive case that mattered. Two equal charges against one credit is
ambiguous and is skipped, the same rule the transfer reconciler uses for ties.

Both halves get a new `excluded` type, keeping their natural signs. Nothing was
needed to keep them out of the totals: all 21 stats sites filter *for*
income/fixed_expense/variable_expense rather than filtering transfers out, so an
unrecognised type drops out by construction. The rows stay visible, so the ledger
still mirrors the statement and can be reconciled against the bank.

Dropping the rows was considered and rejected: the re-billed installments are
imported too (496.04 + 736.67 + 1029.33, exactly a third of the 6786.12 of
reversals), so deleting only the reversal would count each purchase twice.

Closed every edit path that could break a pair: `excluded` is absent from the
create form and the inline type select, the inline controller is not attached to
those rows, and Updater rejects amount and type changes on them. Category and
notes stay editable.

Mobile degrades gracefully — getBadge returns null by default and getAmountVariant
keys off the sign — so an excluded row shows without a badge until its TypeScript
union is updated. Logged separately.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
